extracted.intended_audience: readers of history/biography and scholars of 18th-century Prussian education
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes the schooling regulations and evaluative criteria used by King Friedrich Wilhelm for educating the Crown-Prince (early-18th-century Prussia), including curriculum priorities, daily timetable, disciplinary rules, and pedagogical principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious instruction: love and fear of God
rubrics_metrics.description: Must impress my Son with a proper love and fear of God, as the foundation and sole pillar of our temporal and eternal welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No false religions or sects (Atheist, Arian, Socinian, etc.) are to be named in his hearing; communicate a proper abhorrence of Papistry (UNGRUND UND ABSURDITAT). Teach the 'true religion' — e.g., that Christ died for all men — and the omnipresence of Divine justice as means to keep a sovereign in the right way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language instruction: no Latin; French and German instead
rubrics_metrics.description: "He is to learn no Latin"; instead learn French and German to write and speak "with brevity and propriety."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The King objects to wasted years on 'dead old Heathen Latins'; priority is practical modern languages useful in life. Also practice writing French letters to acquire a good stylum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum focus on useful knowledge (reject useless)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let him learn Arithmetic, Mathematics, Artillery, Economy to the very bottom; in short, useful knowledge generally; useless ditto not at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Friedrich Wilhelm's chief peculiarity is 'ruthless contempt of Useless Knowledge' and insistence on useful, practical instruction that serves state/military ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: History instruction: emphasize recent and domestic history
rubrics_metrics.description: History in particular; Ancient History only slightly (NUR UBERHIN); but the History of the last hundred and fifty Years to the exactest pitch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus especially on the history of the house of Brandenburg and countries connected with it (England, Brunswick, Hessen, etc.). When reading wise history-books, make considerations upon the causes of events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal/political foundations: mastery of jus naturale and jus gentium
rubrics_metrics.description: The JUS NATURALE and JUS GENTIUM must be completely master of; as also of Geography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These legal principles are presented as a 'hand-lamp' to History — conceptual tools to interpret historical and international affairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military education and orientation toward soldier profession
rubrics_metrics.description: With increasing years, go upon Fortification, the Formation of a Camp, and the other War-Sciences; train from youth to act as Officer and General and seek glory in the soldier profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tutors (Finkenstein, Kalkstein) are charged to 'stamp into him a true love for the Soldier business' and impress that glory comes from the sword — manifests in drills, cadet company, miniature arsenal, artillery practice, and engineer lessons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily schedule and strict timetable
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed hour-by-hour schedule (Sunday and weekdays) prescribing wake times, prayers, study blocks, audience with the King, and bedtimes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Sunday rise at 7, bedside prayer aloud, family worship; weekdays called at 6, morning prayers, 7–9 history, 9–10:45 religion, 11–2 with the King, 2–3 maps/geography, 3–4 morality, 4–5 German letter writing, bed by half-past 10. All tasks to be done 'rapidly' (GESCHWINDE/HURTIG) within set minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public/visible prayer to prevent deception
rubrics_metrics.description: Prayer at bedside to be audible to all in the room so 'there be no deception or short measure palmed upon us.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religious observance is to be public and demonstrable; family worship with servants and Duhan to read a Bible chapter and sing psalms is mandated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hygiene, dressing, and self-sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Accustom him to get out of and into his clothes as fast as possible; learn to put on and take off his clothes himself; be clean and neat, 'not so dirty.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific rules: wake promptly (do not loiter), wash quickly (weekday washing without soap in morning), be combed and queued, not powdered on weekdays; dressing/undressing speed is emphasized and monitored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memory practice: rote learning in small doses
rubrics_metrics.description: Intercalate 'a little getting by heart of something, in order to strengthen the memory.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The King prescribes small amounts of memorization to 'strengthen the memory,' but the narrator notes this is likely 'very little.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral instruction and clerical catechism
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular instruction in Christian religion and morality (Noltenius, Panzendorf give clerical drill); questionings from Noltenius's Catechism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religion lessons occupy defined slots (e.g., 9 till quarter to 11) and include catechism recitation; morality is explicitly scheduled (e.g., 3–4 PM).

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing and stylistic training
rubrics_metrics.description: Write German letters with him and see that he gets a good STYLUM; also practice writing French letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular supervised composition practice (e.g., 4–5 PM) aimed at brevity and propriety in expression; the King laments the Prince 'never in the least did' attain the stylum he wanted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geography and strategic knowledge of countries
rubrics_metrics.description: Maps and Geography, giving account of all European Kingdoms; their strength and weakness; size, riches and poverty of their towns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geography is taught to inform strategic/military and political understanding — knowledge of notable features of each country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weekly assessment and remedial study
rubrics_metrics.description: Saturday forenoon: History, Writing and Ciphering; especially repetition of what was done through the week and in MORALITY to see whether he has profited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Fritz has profited, the afternoon is free. If he has not profited, he must, from 2 to 6, repeat and learn rightly what he has forgotten — explicit remedial schedule monitored by senior tutors (Graf Finkenstein and Colonel Kalkstein).

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical and practical arts instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction from riding-masters, fencing-masters, swimming-masters, dancing-masters, music-masters; military drill and miniature artillery practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes a 'little arsenal' for mounting batteries, firing small ordnance under an Engineer-Major, and drill by an experienced drill-master (Rentzel); musical lessons (e.g., flute, Graun on organ) also present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frugality and financial accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Exiguous pocket-money (about eighteenpence a month at start); other incidental moneys laid out under tutor sanction and accurately entered in day-books audited by the King.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Daily life modeled on frugality: restrained allowances, strict accounting for small expenditures (shoes on the last, hair-tape, drink-money, mending flute, collection-plate), and moral praise for simple subsistence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical exposure to military life and inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: Take the Crown-Prince with the King on annual reviews; travel across Prussia visiting garrisons, marching-regiments, and management boards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exposure trains the prince to 'look into everything like a Rhadamanthine Argus' and learn how the master's eye influences outcomes; complements classroom military instruction with field experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of tutors: practitioners not hypocrites
rubrics_metrics.description: The Prince must not be taught by 'Hypocrites, and even Sincere-Hypocrites'; rather by 'real Men, who believed from the heart outwards, and were daily doing what they taught.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrator stresses the advantage of tutors who practice what they preach, and of keeping the pupil's affections alive (sunshine) so instruction may succeed; warns against pedagogues who are mere pedants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional/affective pedagogy: keep affections alive
rubrics_metrics.description: Although rigorous, tutors must be 'not unlovable' so that the pupil's affections remain alive; affection ('sunshine') helps any seed of learning succeed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text contrasts stern routine with the benefit of genial teachers (like Duhan) who open the boy's mind and encourage lively perception — an antidote to purely mechanical instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of small collective military unit for instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Institution of a miniature Soldier Company (Kompagnie der Kronprinzlichen Kadetten) — a hundred and ten boys selected as a tiny regiment for the prince to learn exercise in fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides peer-based drill, discipline and early leadership opportunities; commanded by an experienced Lieutenant-Colonel and a drill-master (Rentzel) to inculcate practical drills and camaraderie.
